title: TETRA events
description: Validated against the complete event object (envelope included). tetra.cell is sent when the serving cell is first seen and whenever what is known about it changes; calls produce one tetra.call.start and one tetra.call.end (same call id and fields, plus the outcome). Subscriber numbers (SSI) are 24 bit; for a group call dst is the group (GSSI).

call.description: Id of the call (its start time in Unix ms and the call identifier, or the traffic channel when the set-up was missed).

cid.description: Call identifier of the CMCE signalling (14 bit, reused by the network).

usage.description: Traffic channel (usage marker) the voice is on.

dst.description: Called party: the GSSI of a group call, the subscriber of an individual call.

src.description: Calling party named by the set-up.

talker.description: Party that last got the right to transmit.

encrypted.description: The air interface encryption flag was seen on the call's PDUs. Nothing is decrypted.

dl_hz.description: Downlink main carrier from the system information.

encryption.description: What the system information announces: no air interface encryption, or it is on (class 2 / 3), or not known yet.

encrypted_traffic_seen.description: A PDU with an encryption mode other than clear was seen on this cell.

services.description: Service details of the BS, named.

voice_ms.description: Voice seen on the air (60 ms per traffic slot).

audio_ms.description: Voice handed to the codec, so what could be heard.

muted.description: True when audio was withheld (encrypted call).

detail.description: The network's notification text for a release.

protocol.description: Protocol identifier as the decoder printed it.

info.description: The decoder's one-line description of the message.
